The values of frequency density for each range can be read off the \(y\) axis of the graph.


Then using the relationship: \(\mathsf{frequency \ density} = \frac{\mathsf{frequency}}{\mathsf{range \ width}}\)

The frequency of each range can be found as the product of the width of the range and the frequency density.

truefeedback.text:
Here is a worked solution:

The total number of calls is equal to the sum of the frequencies over each range.

\({@tans1@} + {@tans3@} + {@tans5@} + {@tans7@} + {@tans9@} + {@tans11@} = {@tans13@}\).

Your answer is not the correct total number of calls.
However it is consistent with the answers you have to part (a).

You have summed the frequency densities for each range.
However, you should have summed the frequencies to find the total number of calls.

Here is a worked solution:

To find the number of calls which were over an hour long, you need to find the frequency of the range \(60 < t \leq 120\).
This can be split up into whole ranges in the table from (a), and the range \(60 < t \leq {@if second(first(data))>60 then second(first(data)) else if second(second(data))>60 then second(second(data)) else if second(third(data))>60 then second(third(data)) else if second(fourth(data))>60 then second(fourth(data)) else if second(fifth(data))>60 then second(fifth(data)) else if second(sixth(data))>60 then second(sixth(data))@}\).

For the range \(60 < t \leq {@if second(first(data))>60 then second(first(data)) else if second(second(data))>60 then second(second(data)) else if second(third(data))>60 then second(third(data)) else if second(fourth(data))>60 then second(fourth(data)) else if second(fifth(data))>60 then second(fifth(data)) else if second(sixth(data))>60 then second(sixth(data))@}\), the frequency of calls can be estimated by calculating the area of the box in the histogram bounded by this range.
Using this, the number of calls in this range is \({@if second(first(data))>60 then second(first(data))-60 else if second(second(data))>60 then second(second(data))-60 else if second(third(data))>60 then second(third(data))-60 else if second(fourth(data))>60 then second(fourth(data))-60 else if second(fifth(data))>60 then second(fifth(data))-60 else if second(sixth(data))>60 then 60@} \times {@if second(first(data))>60 then third(first(data)) else if second(second(data))>60 then third(second(data)) else if second(third(data))>60 then third(third(data)) else if second(fourth(data))>60 then third(fourth(data)) else if second(fifth(data))>60 then third(fifth(data)) else if second(sixth(data))>60 then third(sixth(data))@} = {@if second(first(data))>60 then (second(first(data))-60)*tans2 else if second(second(data))>60 then (second(second(data))-60)*tans4 else if second(third(data))>60 then (second(third(data))-60)*tans6 else if second(fourth(data))>60 then (second(fourth(data))-60)*tans8 else if second(fifth(data))>60 then (second(fifth(data))-60)*tans10 else if second(sixth(data))>60 then 60*tans12@}\).

Therefore, the total number of calls in the range \(60 < t \leq 120\) is: \({@if second(first(data))>60 then sconcat((second(first(data))-60)*tans2, "+", tans3, "+", tans5, "+", tans7, "+", tans9, "+", tans11) else if second(second(data))>60 then sconcat((second(second(data))-60)*tans4, "+", tans5, "+", tans7, "+", tans9, "+", tans11) else if second(third(data))>60 then sconcat((second(third(data))-60)*tans6, "+", tans7, "+", tans9, "+", tans11) else if second(fourth(data))>60 then sconcat((second(fourth(data))-60)*tans8, "+", tans9, "+", tans11) else if second(fifth(data))>60 then sconcat((second(fifth(data))-60)*tans10, "+", tans11) else if second(sixth(data))>60 then 60*tans12@} = {@tans14@}\).

Your answer is not the correct number of calls which are longer than an hour.
However it is consistent with the answers you have to part (a).

You have included all of the calls in the \({@if second(first(data))>60 then 0 else if second(second(data))>60 then first(second(data)) else if second(third(data))>60 then first(third(data)) else if second(fourth(data))>60 then first(fourth(data)) else if second(fifth(data))>60 then first(fifth(data)) else if second(sixth(data))>60 then first(sixth(data))@} < x \leq {@if second(first(data))>60 then first(second(data)) else if second(second(data))>60 then first(third(data)) else if second(third(data))>60 then first(fourth(data)) else if second(fourth(data))>60 then first(fifth(data)) else if second(fifth(data))>60 then first(sixth(data)) else if second(sixth(data))>60 then 120@}\) range.
However, only some of the calls within this range are longer than an hour.
